recipes.name: Steak Chili
ingredients_raw: 2 pounds steak - cut into 1 inch cubes

steps.text: In a large pot over medium high heat, combine the oil and steak and saute for about 5 minutes, or until steak is browned. Add the onions, garlic and chile pepper and saute for another 5 minutes, or until the onions are translucent.

Add the chili powder, cumin, cayenne pepper, tomatoes and kidney beans. Reduce heat to low, cover and simmer for about one hour. Remove cover and simmer for another 30 minutes, or until you've reached your desired thickness.

raw_recipe.headline: Steak Chili
raw_recipe.description: Browned cubes of steak are sauteed with chopped onions, garlic and jalapeno peppers in this kidney bean chili seasoned with cumin and chili powder.

review.reviewBody: This chili was really good after some modifications... Instead of the chili pepper i used a jalepeno pepper, then i used two cans of kidney beans instead of one, and then one tbsp of chili powder instead of two. I didnt have ground cayenne pepper, so instead i substituted cayenne pepper sauce 1 tsp. Definately the best chili I have had.

So I've made this recipes several times. Each time I use a different cut of meat to see how it goes. I've used sirloin, stew meat, and roast. I liked all of them, however I think the sirloin was the best. I did tune this a bit and used some beef broth during the browning process and added some "better than bullion" to ratchet up the flavor. I did add some powdered ghost, reaper, and habaneros...cuz I like it hot! I used black beans instead of kidneys...much better in my opinion. I never serve this on the day I make it. I found that the tomato acids help break the sinew and connective tissues much better is you let it sit overnight. I have done this both refrigerated and at room temperature. The next day I heat it back up and it's just wonderful. I served with sliced habaneros and shredded Mexican style cheese. What a great comfort food! Make this....you won't be disappointed! Lastly, I use a cast iron Dutch Oven, which I believe makes everything better.

This recipe is a winner. I’ve been making chili with cubed chuck roast for over 30 years. I pressure cook the roast beef and/or pork steak (see below) to shorten the cooking time. I also add ground beef and ground pork. I brown the ground meat with onions and drain. If I find pork steak at a good price I’ll cube and pressure cooker that as well.

We added an extra can or beans just to make it more outside friendly!!
I made the steak chunks a bit too big, I wish I would have thought about a hearty spoonful as I was slicing.
I made a day ahead, left it in the warming drawer overnight for tailgating at the game. We placed it on the side of the BBQ for final heat-up and it turned out terrific.

Four stars for this “base” recipe. I added a 12 oz can of Yuengling Lager, about a Tbsp of vegetable Better Than Bullion, some fresh-roasted poblano chile, extra water for the bullion paste, and at the end, a slurry of masa harina and water to thicken.

Added 2 hot peppers as suggested by others and used one 28oz can of tomatoes and one 10 0z can of baked beans. Cooked in the slow cooker for great full flavour. Keeper for when I have frozen beef that needs to be eaten.

Pretty good chili- I really enjoyed the steak (I don't care much for ground meats). I used a sirloin steak- wasn't sure what cut to use, so I just got was on sale. I cut the recipe in half and put it in the crockpot all day. I was going to sear the meat first, but I didn't have time. Instead of a green chile, I used a can of diced tomatoes with green chiles. I added a small can of tomato sauce because it seemed too thick at first, but at the end it was almost too thin- I left the lid off the crockpot for a while so it would thicken up. I added 1/2 green bell pepper and used one can of pinto beans. Served with light sour cream, cheese, and Honey Corn Bread from this site. A hearty, very filling meal!

This is my wife's main request. I make it in a slow cooker for 6 to 8 hours. We prefer 3 lbs. of tri-tip cut into tiny pieces, and omit the beans and use only one sweet onion. The last little bit I do differently is put a couple of handfulls of very thin tortilla chips in a food processor and add that in to cook. A little trick I learned online... it makes it a little thicker and adds just the right amount of salt.

To start, I just brown the meat, then saute the onion and chili separately, adding the garlic in for the last minute. Lastly the spices, exactly as the recipe.

super yum...I highly recommend tri-tip... freeze it for a couple of hours first and you'll have perfectly nice little chunks that simply melt in your mouth!

So easy. I cooked a cheap piece of London Broil in slow cooker. When tender enough, I shredded meat, added spices along with a can of Guinness. We like spicy, so I used a can of fire tomatoes and can of Rotel. It was a little thin so I add a corn starch paste. Very good. Next time I will use green chilies. Keeper.

We used just one onion, one large and one small can of diced tomatoes, and one can of Rotel. Instead of chili powder, we used a packet of chili mix, but I still added salt and pepper (1/4 tsp), cumin as called for in the recipe here, and two rather than three cloves of garlic. I simmered mine for two hours in the Dutch oven and found that the moisture was perfect right off the stove (rather than the next day). Enjoy!
The recipe is good, but for a more tender meal, the steak should cook longer, and then add the beans; maybe in a crock pot. I will try that next time!
I think it has too much chili powder. Maybe use 2 teaspoons not 2 tablespoons.

Tastes great now..know it will be fantastic in the morning. Boneless bottom blade steak, pickled jalepenos cuz im a canuk and black beans ONLY because i forgot my kidney beans at the bar on the way home. Really impressed.
It was definitely worth the time and the effort. I cooked it for a little less time and it was still good. I warmed some bread for dipping. This is a chili that I will make again
"This is the best chili I've ever had. I get requests for this all the time." Regular guests for dinner or a food bank donor?
I love how easy it was to put together. I did add some smoked paprika, garlic and onion powder just to bump up the flavor. I cook with little to no salt, so the extra punch of flavor was needed

We enjoyed this recipe, with a simple minor tweak. The chili is simple, with basic ingredients and I love the use of steak instead of ground beef. I ended up using a "chili grind" of beef that my butcher sells. It's much coarser than ground beef, but a bit finer that cubed up steak. The only thing I suggest is adding salt. There is none at all in the recipe (it comes out pretty bland), and it needs it to make the flavors pop. Start with 1 teaspoon and go from there.
